content.value_statement: Prompt quality often fails because requirements, examples, and evaluation criteria are unclear. This skill helps teams design, test, and review production prompts for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Provides prompt patterns for structured output, RAG queries, few-shot examples, and reasoning tasks.
Guides LLM evaluation planning with metrics, test cases, and production review criteria.
Describes agentic system design topics such as resource awareness, caching, access control, and observability.
Includes Python script stubs for prompt optimization, RAG evaluation, and agent orchestration workflows.
Offers examples for customer feedback, coding assistant, and support agent prompt design.
limitations: The Python scripts are scaffolds and do not implement deep optimization or evaluation logic.
The reference documents provide broad guidance, not a complete production framework.
The skill does not call LLM APIs or automatically measure model quality.
Deployment command examples require human review before use in real infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Define Prompt Requirements
use_cases.description: Turn product goals into clear prompt instructions, examples, constraints, and acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Plan LLM Evaluations
use_cases.description: Create evaluation cases, success metrics, and failure checks for prompt and RAG workflows.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Designs
use_cases.description: Assess agentic workflows for tool use, observability, access control, and production readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Basic Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this prompt for clarity. Suggest clearer instructions, missing context, and one useful example. Keep the revised prompt concise.

prompt_templates.title: Create Structured Output Instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a prompt that returns named fields in a stable format. Include validation rules and fallback behavior for missing information.

prompt_templates.title: Design a RAG Answering Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a RAG prompt that uses retrieved context, cites sources, handles unknown answers, and avoids unsupported claims.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Evaluation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an evaluation plan for this LLM workflow. Include test categories, scoring criteria, edge cases, and release gates.

output_examples.input: Improve a vague customer feedback prompt.
output: Clear task definition with named feedback categories.
Rules for uncertain or mixed feedback.

output_examples.input: Design a RAG prompt for policy questions.
output: Instructions to answer only from retrieved policy text.
Citation requirements for every factual claim.
Fallback wording when the context is incomplete.

output_examples.input: Review an agent workflow before launch.
output: Tool access risks and approval points.
Evaluation cases for unsafe or ambiguous requests.
Release criteria for human handoff behavior.

best_practices: Start with measurable task goals before adding examples or formatting rules.
Test prompts with realistic edge cases, unclear inputs, and adversarial wording.
Separate prompt instructions from product guardrails, access control, and validation logic.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on vague persona text instead of concrete behavior requirements.
Do not place credentials, private data, or sensitive business rules in reusable prompts.
Do not treat a passing demo as proof of production readiness.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design prompts, evaluation plans, RAG instructions, and agent workflow reviews for LLM applications.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is model-agnostic and can be applied across Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and similar tools.

faq.question: Does it run live model evaluations?
faq.answer: No. It provides evaluation planning guidance and script scaffolds, but it does not call model APIs.

faq.question: Can beginners use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The templates start with basic prompt cleanup and progress toward production evaluation planning.

faq.question: Is this a complete agent framework?
faq.answer: No. It is guidance and scaffolding for designing and reviewing agentic systems.

faq.question: Should I run the deployment commands directly?
faq.answer: No. Treat command examples as documentation and review them before using real infrastructure.
